prompt:
Use case: illustration-story. Asset: one ORIGINAL MASTER painting for one Bhagavad Gita verse in a Sanskrit reader. Generate a single square 1:1 image, 2048x2048 or the highest actually supported native square resolution. Consistent series style: refined traditional Indian watercolor and restrained gouache on warm ivory handmade paper; fine organic detail, subtle ochre, sage, dusty terracotta and muted indigo; dignified ancient Indian setting, quiet atmospheric daylight. The image must illustrate THIS VERSE'S ACTUAL MEANING. Read the exact source meaning below; derive a concrete, intelligible scene or a restrained symbolic interpretation of that teaching. Never simply paint an unrelated chariot, generic temple or anonymous landscape. Compose one coherent scene, no collage or infographic. Keep important faces, hands, relationships and narrative objects inside the central 60% of width and central 50% of height, surrounded by ample low-detail sky, ground and paper atmosphere. No important subject cut by an edge. This one master must support portrait/landscape phones and tablets through safe proportional fitting. No text of any kind, no verse number, no letters, no Sanskrit/Roman typography, no watermark, no frame, no UI. Text will be rendered separately by the app over the image at a user-adjustable default image opacity of 48%. If Krishna is depicted, maintain a youthful calm blue-skinned figure in muted golden-yellow garments, a restrained peacock-feather crown, no modern jewelry. Arjuna is a dark-haired warrior with a small crown, bow and understated bronze armor. Use them only when the meaning warrants them; the scene or analogy remains verse-specific.  Reference (DO NOT DRAW THIS TEXT): Bhagavad Gītā 3.13. Exact Sanskrit: यज्ञशिष्टाशिनः सन्तो मुच्यन्ते सर्वकिल्बिषैः ।
भुञ्जते ते त्वघं पापा ये पचन्त्यात्मकारणात् ॥ १३ ॥ Exact stored meaning: The righteous, who eat the remnants of sacrifice (yajña-śiṣṭa), are freed from all sins. But those sinful ones who cook only for themselves — they eat sin alone. Chapter context: Karma yoga: selfless action, duty, reciprocity, example, desire and restraint. Depict the precise everyday action or analogy described. Do not make every verse an identical Krishna-Arjuna portrait. Previous verse context only, do not substitute for the target: Nourished by sacrifice, the devas will indeed give you your desired enjoyments. One who enjoys their gifts without offering back to them is verily a thief. Next verse context only, do not substitute for the target: Beings arise from food; food arises from rain; rain arises from sacrifice (yajña); sacrifice arises from action (karma). Final instruction: center the distinctive content of the TARGET meaning, not the neighboring verses. No fabricated teaching or unrelated religious scene.
review_note: Contact-sheet inspection; conservative full-frame safe region preserves all figures and objects.

entry.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 3.13: The righteous, who eat the remnants of sacrifice (yajña-śiṣṭa), are freed from all sins. But those sinful ones who cook only for themselves — they eat sin alone.
